procedural_history.impugned_order: Final Judgment and Order dated 29.06.2015 passed by the High Court of Judicature for Rajasthan at Jodhpur in S.B.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court upheld the decision of the District Judge, which had dismissed the claim petition as being time-barred under Article 82 of The Limitation Act, 1963.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellants (original claimants) approached the Supreme Court after the High Court upheld the dismissal of their claim petition.

directions: There shall be no order as to costs.
This order is passed under the peculiar facts of this case and hence, it is not to be treated as a precedent.

issue.issue_text: Whether a claim petition for damages should be governed by the two-year limitation period under Article 82 of the Limitation Act, 1963, or the three-year residuary limitation period under Article 113 of the Act.

facts: The appellants, the widow and son of the deceased, filed a claim for damages under Section 1A of the Fatal Accidents Act, 1855.
The claim was filed more than two years but less than three years after the date of death.
The lower courts dismissed the claim, holding that it was barred by the two-year limitation period under Article 82 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
The appellants argued that the claim should be treated as a civil suit for damages, and therefore the three-year residuary limitation period under Article 113 should apply.
law: The Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963, is divided into parts for different types of suits.
Part VII of the Schedule deals with "suits relating to tort".
Article 82, which falls under Part VII, specifically provides a two-year limitation period for suits filed under the Fatal Accidents Act, 1855.
Article 113 is a residuary article that provides a three-year limitation period for suits for which no specific period of limitation is provided elsewhere in the Schedule.
application: The Court identified that the claim for damages was brought under the Fatal Accidents Act, 1855, which is a suit relating to tort.
It found that the Limitation Act provides a specific entry, Article 82, which explicitly sets a two-year limitation period for this exact type of suit.
The Court applied the legal principle that a residuary article, like Article 113, can only be invoked when no specific limitation period is provided for a particular type of suit.
Since Article 82 specifically covers suits under the Fatal Accidents Act, 1855, the residuary Article 113 cannot be applied.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that a claim petition for damages under the Fatal Accidents Act, 1855, is governed by the specific two-year limitation period prescribed under Article 82 of the Limitation Act, 1963, and not the three-year residuary period under Article 113.

arguments.issue_text: Whether a claim petition for damages should be governed by the two-year limitation period under Article 82 of the Limitation Act, 1963, or the three-year residuary limitation period under Article 113 of the Act.
appellant_arguments: The petition filed before the District Judge should be treated as a Civil Suit for damages.
Consequently, the three-year residuary limitation period under Article 113 of the Limitation Act, 1963 should be applied.
The right to sue accrued on the date of death (14.09.2008), and since the petition was filed on 05.09.2011, it was within the three-year time limit.
The appellants cited the decision in Jay Laxmi Salt Works (P) Ltd. v. State of Gujarat to support their argument that Article 113 should be applied.
respondent_arguments: The claim should have been presented within the two-year limitation period as prescribed by Article 82 of the Limitation Act, 1963.

statutes.section: Article 82, Part VII of the Schedule

ratio_decidendi.ratio: This case establishes no binding legal rule, as the court explicitly directed that the order is not to be treated as a precedent.
obiter: Part VII of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963, which provides the period of limitation for suits relating to tort, governs claims for compensation arising from death under Article 82.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The court concluded that the contentions raised by the appellants could not be appreciated because Part VII of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963, specifically deals with the period of limitation for suits relating to tort, and Article 82, which prescribes a two-year limitation period for claims under the Fatal Accidents Act, 1855, falls under this specific part.
legal_tests_applied: Application of the principle that a specific provision in a statute (Article 82 of the Limitation Act, 1963, under Part VII dealing with torts) prevails over a general or residuary provision (Article 113).
why_appellant_lost: The court rejected the appellant's argument that their petition should be treated as a general Civil Suit for damages governed by the residuary Article 113, stating, 'We are afraid the contentions raised by the appellants cannot be appreciated.'

The court found that the claim falls squarely under Part VII of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963, which deals with suits relating to tort, and therefore the specific provision of Article 82 applies.
The precedent cited by the appellants, Jay Laxmi Salt Works (P) Ltd. v. State of Gujarat, was held to be inapplicable to the facts of the case.
why_respondent_won: The respondent's contention that the claim should have been presented within the two-year limitation period prescribed by Article 82 of the Limitation Act, 1963, was upheld by the court.
